safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.86 days

narrative: Demand for PL1__M90E32FE is lumpy (CV=1.05, 56% non-zero days) with no detectable trend across the 168-day history. Lead times are short but highly volatile (mean=0.69 days, CV=1.04), driven predominantly by transport variability. The current SAP policy orders at MOQ (239 units) resulting in 108 replenishments per year and excessive ordering costs; switching to EOQ (1,897 units) reduces annual cost by 73% while maintaining 95% service level within 45% of storage capacity.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy but stationary demand with volatile lead times is well-suited to continuous-review (r,Q): the reorder point absorbs uncertainty while the fixed EOQ minimises total annual cost. Periodic review would add unnecessary demand risk in weeks with zero demand followed by spikes.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation after replenishment is 44.6% (2,081 of 4,666 units) — no capacity constraint binds. If safety stock is raised to the robust estimate (220 units), utilisation rises to 44.8%, still well within limits.
